divergences.topic: Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?
divergences.why_it_matters: The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers.
standard_refs: CBUAE HSA Resolution: fees for Letters of Guarantee/Credit (Kafalah)

positions.position: Not permissible to take remuneration for issuing a letter of guarantee, with or without cover, where the remuneration is consideration for the guarantee itself (expense recovery treated separately).
positions.basis: SS 5 text read verbatim from ss1.txt 2026-07-18

positions.position: Permits the fee: the guarantor may charge for the kafalah service, as a fixed amount or a percentage of the guaranteed amount.
positions.basis: BNM Kafalah PD 15.1-15.2, read verbatim 2026-07-17 (20170417-pd-kafalah_130417-revised.txt)

positions.position: Resolution 136/6/2020 (10 Dec 2020, effective 1 Jul 2021): the issuing bank 'may charge an amount equal to the value of actual expenses'; additional amounts only within the stated parameters, and 'it is impermissible to charge an additional amount above the Actual Expenses in exchange for issuing a Guarantee if the Guarantee resulted into a loan' — such excess must be returned to the client or transferred to charity; fees must not be 'a pretext to collect interest (riba)'.
positions.basis: centralbank.ae official PDF (HSA Resolution 136/6/2020, parameters for LG/LC fees), read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Classical Hanafi architecture of kafalah (Kasani, Bada'i) treats it in the guarantee framework the AAOIFI prohibition rests on; explicit school-level fee statement pending a direct citation.
positions.basis: kafalah_v4.json K016 (structure only — fee statement not in the quoted passage)

positions.position: Fee for the guarantee itself impermissible — al-Hattab (Maliki) quoted: 'Scholars are agreed on the impermissibility of guarantee against conditional payment'; guarantee treated as a gratuitous/charitable contract.
positions.basis: aliftaa.jo/en-fatwas/3474 (Jordan Iftaa', quoting al-Hattab) + UM Journal of Shariah Law Research kafalah-bil-ujr article, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Among the four schools reported unanimous that taking a fee for the guarantee itself is impermissible (guarantee analogized to a loan drawing benefit).
positions.basis: UM Journal of Shariah Law Research kafalah-bil-ujr article — 'jurists of Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali Schools... non-permissibility of taking fee', read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Classical Hanbali treatment (Ibn Qudama, al-Mughni 5:71) records the guarantee's validity across schools; explicit fee statement pending a direct citation.
positions.basis: kafalah_v4.json K017 (structure only)

positions.position: Sistani: 'it is permissible for the bank to receive commission from the contractor in return for standing guarantor', characterized as a sort of ju'alah — the live counter-position to the Sunni-schools prohibition.
positions.basis: sistani.org, Current Legal Issues (english-book-45.pdf), read 2026-07-25.

divergences.why_it_matters: The most contested liquidity tool; bodies and jurisdictions genuinely split.

positions.position: Resolution 179 (19/5), Sharjah, April 2009: organized and reverse (banking) tawarruq impermissible; classical form permitted with conditions.
positions.basis: web-verified 2026-07-17, official IIFA publication

positions.position: Permitted but restricted: need-based, not a financing mode of first resort; commodity must be sold to a third party — 'inah strictly prohibited (4/5).
positions.basis: SS 30 clauses 3/1, 4/1, 4/5, 5/1 read verbatim 2026-07-17 (ss2.txt)

positions.position: Bursa Suq al-Sila' (launched 17 Aug 2009, developed with BNM and the SC) is the official 'platform that conducts commodity trading transactions, especially in Islamic banking transactions involving Tawarruq or Commodity Murabahah contracts' — organized tawarruq operates at national-exchange scale in Malaysia.
positions.basis: my.bursamalaysia.com BSAS introduction page, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Contested WITHIN the school: individual tawarruq recorded/permitted in later Hanbali manuals (al-Bahuti, Sharh Muntaha); opposed by Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Qayyim.
positions.basis: terms T001/T164 earliest_source citations (standard attributions)

positions.position: Individual tawarruq (sale to a third party) permitted by the Hanafi mainstream (Ibn al-Humam, Ibn Abidin cited), while bilateral inah is condemned.
positions.basis: Habib Ahmed, Durham repository tawarruq paper, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Tawarruq permissible 'as long as there is no interference by the first seller in the second sale'.
positions.basis: Habib Ahmed, Durham repository tawarruq paper, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Early Shafi'is (al-Shafi'i, al-Mawardi) permitted even inah, a fortiori tawarruq; later Shafi'is deem such sales disliked though valid.
positions.basis: Habib Ahmed, Durham repository tawarruq paper, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Position pending a direct citation.

Recognises organized/banking tawarruq as a permissible product structure, with conditions: strict contract sequence, real identifiable deliverable asset (gold/silver/currencies/debt excluded), possession before onward sale, agency permitted, and 'the tawarruq shall not contain any condition that requires the purchaser to promise that the asset will be sold to its original seller' (18.3).
positions.basis: BNM Tawarruq PD reissued 28 Dec 2018 (BNM/RH/PD 028-8), official document read via islamicbankers.center mirror 2026-07-25.

positions.position: IFSB's guidance note on Commodity Murabahah Transactions treats CMT as an accepted, widely used liquidity-management tool and sets its risk/capital treatment — the standards-body counterweight to IIFA Resolution 179's prohibition.
positions.basis: GN-2 title/scope confirmed via IFSB-23 abbreviations list + IFSB TN-5 footnote (ifsb.org PDFs), read 2026-07-25. GN-2 paragraph-level text not yet read (green/on disk — standards_kb_new_batch_2.json): pull clause to upgrade.

divergences.topic: Late-payment charge — income for the bank, or charity only?
divergences.why_it_matters: Every deferred-sale demo must show where a late fee goes.

positions.position: Any charity payment against defaults and delayed payments by the customer shall not be recognised as an income of the seller and shall be taken directly to charity payable, when received.
positions.basis: FAS 28 para 38, read verbatim 2026-07-20 (57b365f3-FAS28MurabahaandOtherDeferredPaymentSales...txt)

divergences.topic: Bay' al-'inah (sale and buy-back) — Malaysia-permitted vs Gulf-prohibited
divergences.why_it_matters: The sharpest jurisdiction split in Islamic finance: the same two-leg structure is a regulated product in Malaysia and a void riba stratagem under AAOIFI.
standard_refs: SC Malaysia SAC resolution on bai' 'inah (5th meeting 29 Jan 1997; revised resolution effective 1 Oct 2014)
BNM SAC circular on bai' 'inah (19 Dec 2012)

positions.position: A murabaha later discovered to have been carried out through buy-back arrangements is void as tantamount to 'inah; the customer must not sell an item to the institution and then repurchase it (clause 2/2/3).
positions.basis: SS 8 clause 2/2/3 read verbatim from full-text reproduction (pkic.com SS-8 PDF) 2026-07-25 — 'this would render the transaction void as it is tantamount to Inah'. Upgrade: confirm against on-disk Standards file.

positions.position: 1997: 'bai` `inah is a principle that is permissible in the Islamic capital market in Malaysia' (contracts judged by disclosed terms, adopting the Shafi'i view). Revised resolution effective 1 Oct 2014 tightened it: two clear and separate contracts, any repurchase condition annuls the contract, simultaneous execution annuls both, and 'the practice of pre-signing of legal documents for bai` `inah transaction is not allowed'.
positions.basis: sc.com.my official PDFs: SAC Resolutions 2nd ed. 2006 (5th meeting, 29 Jan 1997) + Resolutions compilation 31 Dec 2020 (revised bai' 'inah resolution), read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Permitted inah from 1998 (interbank money market, Shafi'i mechanism, non-ribawi commodity); 2012 circular imposed five strict conditions (two clear separate agreements, no repurchase obligation term, different execution times, correct sequence, effective ownership transfer) — banks that cannot comply 'are not allowed to offer financial products and services based on bai' inah'.
positions.basis: BNM SAC Resolutions compilation 2007 (8th meeting 12 Dec 1998; 18th meeting 12 Apr 2001) + BNM circular 'Implementation of SAC of BNM's Resolution on Bai' Inah' 19 Dec 2012, official documents read via islamicbankers.center mirror 2026-07-25 (bnm.gov.my robots-blocked).

positions.position: Bilateral inah condemned — Muhammad al-Shaybani: 'I hate this sale so much and it is the invention of those who eat riba'; later Hanafis permit only the tripartite form (via a third party).

positions.position: Prohibited where the resale is arranged with the first seller — a riba stratagem blocked under sadd al-dhara'i (al-Qarafi: 'we only forbid when the second sale is arranged by the first seller').
positions.basis: Habib Ahmed, Durham repository tawarruq paper (quoting al-Qarafi), read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: Contract valid judged by its external form — al-Shafi'i (al-Umm 3/78) authorized it, intention left to God; later Shafi'is deem it disliked though legally valid.

divergences.topic: Bay' al-dayn — selling debt to a third party at a discount

positions.position: Resolution 101 (4/11): 'It is not permissible to sell, to a third party, any immature debt for an early-paid amount of money, whether in the same currency of the debt or any other currency.' divergences.topic: Wa'd and muwa'adah — when does a promise become a binding contract?
divergences.why_it_matters: Promises hold together murabaha, hedging and sukuk exits; a binding bilateral promise is one step from a forward contract.

positions.position: Resolutions 40-41 (2/5, 3/5), Kuwait 1988: a unilateral promise is 'morally binding on the promisor, unless there is a valid excuse' and legally binding if made conditional and the promisee incurred expenses. 'Mutual promise is permissible in the case of Murabahah sale provided that the option is given to one or both parties. Without such an option, it is not permissible' — a binding muwa'adah resembles the sale itself, which requires the seller's possession.
positions.basis: iifa-aifi.org/en/32332.html, read 2026-07-25.

positions.position: 'A bilateral promise to perform an act that is prohibited by the Shari'ah is itself prohibited' (4/1 — e.g. structures circumventing riba). Fulfilling a permitted bilateral promise is a religious obligation 'but is not legally binding except in situations where an actual commercial transaction is not possible without a binding bilateral promise' due to legal requirements or commercial custom, and the objective is not merely financing (4/2; named applications: documentary credits, supply agreements).
positions.basis: SS 49 clauses 4/1, 4/2 read verbatim from full-text reproduction (pkic.com SS-49 PDF) 2026-07-25. Upgrade: confirm against on-disk Standards file. Note: currency hedging is NOT named in the fetched SS 49 text.
